# Contributing

Thanks for helping improve `contentful.py`.

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Version | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Python | 3.9–3.13 | Source: `pyproject.toml → requires-python` |
| PDM | Latest | Install with `pip install pdm`; manages deps, lock, and build |
| Docker | Latest | Required for the devcontainer workflow |
| Dev Container CLI | Latest | `npm install -g @devcontainers/cli@0`; used to run the devcontainer locally |

No `.nvmrc` or Node version pinning applies — this is a pure Python repo.

## Getting Started

### Using Dev Containers (recommended)

This repository ships a `.devcontainer/` configuration that creates a reproducible Python environment and auto-installs all dependencies. CI runs in the same container, so "works locally but not in CI" drift is eliminated.

**Visual Studio Code:**
1. Install the [Dev Containers extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode-remote.remote-containers)
2. Open the repository in VS Code
3. Run `Dev Containers: Reopen in Container`

**Terminal / other editors:**
```bash
# Install Dev Container CLI
npm install -g @devcontainers/cli@0

# Start the container and open a shell
devcontainer up --workspace-folder .
devcontainer exec --workspace-folder . bash
```

The `postCreateCommand` in `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` runs `pdm install -G test && python -m pip install -e .` automatically.

### Manual Setup

```bash
git clone git@github.com:contentful/contentful.py.git
cd contentful.py

# Install dependencies (test group)
pdm install -G test

# Install package in editable mode
python -m pip install -e .
```

## Commands

All commands are sourced from `pyproject.toml → [tool.pdm.scripts]` unless noted.

### Testing

```bash
pdm run test           # source: pyproject.toml → scripts.test — runs: python -m unittest discover
pdm run coverage       # source: pyproject.toml → scripts.coverage — runs tests + coverage report
pdm run test-all       # source: pyproject.toml → scripts.test-all — runs: tox (all Python versions)
```

### Linting

```bash
pdm run lint           # source: pyproject.toml → scripts.lint — runs: flake8 .
```

### Combined verification (matches CI)

```bash
pdm run lint && pdm run coverage
```

### Cleaning artifacts

```bash
pdm run clean          # source: pyproject.toml → scripts.clean — removes build/, dist/, .egg-info, .tox/, .coverage, htmlcov/
pdm run clean-build    # source: pyproject.toml → scripts.clean-build
pdm run clean-pyc      # source: pyproject.toml → scripts.clean-pyc
pdm run clean-test     # source: pyproject.toml → scripts.clean-test
```

### Documentation

```bash
pdm run docs           # source: pyproject.toml → scripts.docs — builds Sphinx HTML docs to docs/; opens in browser
```

## Development Workflow

Tests do not hit live APIs — they use VCR cassettes (YAML fixtures in `fixtures/`). You can run the full suite offline:

```bash
# Run all tests
pdm run test

# Run a single test file
python -m unittest tests.client_test

# Run a specific test case
python -m unittest tests.client_test.ClientTest.test_some_method
```

If you add a new endpoint or change HTTP behavior, record a new cassette:
- VCR is configured in the test via `@vcr.use_cassette('fixtures/...')` decorators
- To re-record: delete the cassette file and run the test with live credentials (set `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` and `CONTENTFUL_ACCESS_TOKEN` — not required for existing cassettes)

## Testing

- **Framework:** Python `unittest` (standard library)
- **Location:** `tests/*_test.py`
- **HTTP mocking:** VCR (`vcrpy`) — cassettes live in `fixtures/` organized by endpoint category
- **Run all:** `pdm run test`
- **Run with coverage:** `pdm run coverage`
- **Cross-version matrix:** `pdm run test-all` (runs `tox` across Python 3.9–3.13)
- **Coverage config:** `pyproject.toml → [tool.coverage]` — covers the `contentful/` package with branch tracking

## Code Style & Conventions

- **Linter:** `flake8` — config in `.flake8`; max line length 180, max complexity 10
- **No formatter configured** — no Prettier or Black enforced; defer to flake8
- **Field naming:** External API names are camelCase; internal Python attributes use `snake_case` via `contentful/utils.py::snake_case()`
- **Docstrings:** Public methods in `client.py` use Google-style docstrings with `:param:`, `:return:`, `:rtype:`, and usage examples

## Commit Convention

This repo uses [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/):

```
type(scope): description
```

Valid types: `feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `perf`, `ci`, `build`, `revert`

Examples from git history:
```
feat: add support for taxonomy concept schemes and metadata (#111)
fix: correct formatting in README for embargoed assets section (#103)
chore: add devcontainer contributor workflow [DX-822] (#116)
chore(ci): [SECURITY-936] Enable CodeQL scans for GitHub workflow (#108)
```

## Branch Strategy

- `master` — default branch
- Feature branches — create from `master`, open a PR against `master`

## Pull Requests

1. Fork the repository (external contributors) or create a branch (team members)
2. Create a branch for your change
3. Run `pdm run lint && pdm run coverage` inside the devcontainer to verify
4. Open a PR against `master` with a short summary of the change and any follow-up context
5. CI runs lint and test across Python 3.9–3.13 in the devcontainer — all checks must pass

Source: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

## Sensitive Files & Paths

| Path | Why restricted |
|---|---|
| `pdm.lock` | Auto-generated — do not hand-edit; use `pdm lock` or `pdm install` to regenerate |
| `docs/` | Auto-generated from Sphinx via `pdm run docs` / `pdm run git-docs` — do not hand-edit |
| `contentful/__init__.py → __version__` | Version source of truth for PDM dynamic versioning — update here before releasing |
| `fixtures/**/*.yaml` | VCR cassettes — generated from real API responses. Hand-editing breaks test replay; re-record instead |
